name: Grän
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny village by Haldensee with a natural swimming beach and the Füssener Jöchle ski area.
beschreibung:
Overview

Grän is situated at an elevation of 1,138 metres in the enchanting Tannheimer Tal in the Tyrolean district of Reutte, lying directly adjacent to the Bavarian border. Home to around 600 residents, this sun-drenched mountain municipality comprises the main village of Grän alongside the idyllic hamlets of Haldensee, Innergschwend, and Enge in the romantic Engetal. Celebrated as the sunniest village in the high valley, Grän benefits from a peaceful location away from transit corridors, framed by the dramatic limestone rock faces of the Tannheim climbing peaks such as Rote Flüh, Gimpel, Aggenstein, and the 1,818-metre Füssener Jöchle. The emerald waters of Lake Haldensee spread out at the base of the peaks as one of Tyrol's cleanest mountain lakes. Grän seamlessly unites pristine nature, welcoming hospitality, and year-round active outdoor holidays.

History

The name Grän derives from the Middle High German term Gruon, referring to a green clearing or windblown forest opening. Historical records date back to the Late Middle Ages: the Gräner Älpele alpine pasture was documented in 1459, when a modest timber chapel dedicated to St. Wendelin, protector of shepherds and cattle, already stood in the village. Following a devastating cattle plague in the early 17th century, grateful villagers pledged a permanent stone church, which rapidly flourished into a celebrated regional pilgrimage site. The present Baroque parish church of St. Wendelin was constructed in 1789 by master builder Michael Zobl, crowned with an iconic onion dome. For centuries, the rugged Engetal served as an important packhorse and smuggling route linking Tyrol with the Allgäu, while local folklore still tells the legend of a sunken estate whose flooding formed Lake Haldensee.

Getting There

By car, visitors from Germany reach Grän completely toll-free and without an Austrian motorway vignette via the A7 motorway, taking the Pfronten/Füssen exit and following the scenic Engetal road L261 straight to Grän. Alternatively, travellers can drive from Kempten via Oy-Mittelberg and the Oberjoch Pass along the B199. From the Tyrolean Inn Valley, the route approaches over the Fern Pass to Reutte and up through the Gaicht Pass into the high valley. Rail travellers arrive at Pfronten-Ried in Bavaria or Reutte in Tirol along the Außerfern Railway. From the stations, scheduled VVT bus line 120 runs regular services throughout the Tannheimer Tal, free for guests holding the regional Tannheimer Tal guest card.

Tips

A premier summer highlight is Lake Haldensee and its lakeside Wasserwelt Haldensee waterpark, featuring a solar-heated pool with a 50-metre water slide, sunbathing lawns, rowing boat hire, and a scenic 4.3-kilometre walking loop around the water. The modern 8-seater Füssener Jöchle gondola carries hikers to 1,821 metres altitude and the Sonnenalm restaurant; a short scenic walk leads to the Gamskopf peak, home to the largest summit cross in the valley and distant views toward Neuschwanstein Castle. In winter, the Füssener Jöchle ski area offers nine scenic piste kilometres tailored for families and leisure skiers. Cross-country skiers enjoy direct access to the valley's award-winning 140-kilometre trail network, home to the famous Ski-Trail marathon. Mountain hikers can tackle the challenging ascent to the Bad Kissinger Hütte (1,788 m) on the Aggenstein.
metaDescription: Grän in the Tannheimer Tal: Sunny alpine village on Lake Haldensee, Füssener Jöchle cable car, Wasserwelt water park, and top cross-country skiing.
